questions.text: Why should a newline-delimited JSON-RPC server send diagnostic logs to stderr rather than stdout?

options.A: Because stderr automatically turns log messages into JSON-RPC notifications.
options.B: Because stdout is reserved for requests and stderr for responses.
options.C: Because ordinary log lines on stdout can corrupt the protocol message stream.
options.D: Because stderr guarantees that log messages cannot contain sensitive data.

questions.explanation: The client reads stdout as protocol messages. Ordinary diagnostic text can break parsing; stderr keeps it outside that message stream.

questions.text: A resource response contains one user’s private note body. Which cache policy fits the lesson’s guidance?

options.A: Mark it public so any authenticated client can reuse it.
options.B: Mark it private and prevent reuse across authorization contexts.
options.C: Mark it public if its URI and list ordering are deterministic.
options.D: Omit cacheScope because a short TTL establishes user isolation.

questions.explanation: User-specific data requires private caching scoped to the appropriate authorization context. A TTL does not establish access isolation.

questions.text: With valid request metadata, tools/call invokes notes_search with arguments={"query":""}. Its executor raises ValueError. How does handle_tools_call return this failure?

options.A: A complete result with isError=True and the error message in content.
options.B: A JSON-RPC error with code -32603 because all executor exceptions escape.
options.C: A successful result with isError=False and an empty list of search hits.
options.D: No response because an empty query changes the request into a notification.

questions.explanation: handle_tools_call catches ValueError from the executor and wraps its message in content with isError=True using complete().
